security_privacy_cost_impact: Data classification synthetic-only; secrets_required false; network policy deny-unless-declared and no network was used. No credential, provider call, migration or customer record is touched, and no fixture carries a real value — the constructed probe documents use ws_synthetic_/usr_synthetic_/usg_synthetic_ identifiers and a `synthetic` provider_key. Cost impact none: no metered resource exists yet, which is why the cost metrics specify what would be computed rather than reporting anything. TWO security-relevant positions are recorded rather than assumed. First, the withdrawn increment asked in two places for CTR-EVT-001.payload to be widened; that ask is WITHDRAWN ENTIRELY. payload at maxProperties 0 is a deliberately closed control of the same family as CTR-AUD-001.details, whose annotation calls a free-form bag 'how a secret or a page of user content reaches an audit log', and the metric never needed it — a step identifier validates today through event_type and subject. Second, one privacy-adjacent position is recorded and not decided: four metrics read CTR-AUD-001, whose retention.policy_ref deliberately pins no duration because PDPA-006 is undelivered, so any window set here must be re-checked against a retention period Privacy/Legal has yet to state.
migration_and_data_impact: None. No schema, migration, table, index or stored record is defined or altered; the dictionary specifies how existing contract fields would be aggregated, and specifying an aggregation creates no data. Two shapes this package deliberately did NOT define: a job lifecycle (CTR-JOB-001 declares no terminal-state field, executed as probe JOB-NO-TERMINAL-STATE, so S-05 is a count rather than an invented rate) and an onboarding step vocabulary (which belongs to CTR-EVT-001's owner).
compatibility_impact: Every file under contract-catalog/ was read and none was written. The eight contracts cited are consumed as the source column of a metric dictionary, not implemented, extended or reinterpreted, so no consumer's compatibility surface moves. The probe script IMPORTS test-kits/contracts/json-schema-subset.mjs and modifies nothing in test-kits/. The one place this package touches a contract's concern is the CTR-OBS-001 per-label cardinality budget, which is RECORDED here and remains unenforced there; that contract's standing constraint against emitting sli_tags to a real metric backend before the budget lands is restated rather than relaxed.
known_limitations: A dictionary is not instrumentation. Twelve of fourteen metrics name a field that exists; none has ever been computed, because no usage, audit, job or notification record has been emitted by anything. Every 'derivable' verdict is a statement about the schema, not about data.

A-03's STATUS IS A DECISION, NOT A FACT, and the Author was instructed to make it and to record both readings. The reason the withdrawn increment gave was false and is corrected: CTR-EVT-001's event_type is an OPEN grammar admitting onboarding.step.completed, and subject is REQUIRED with free-text type and id, so a step-identifying event validates unmodified (probe EVT-CARRIER). The Author nonetheless keeps `absent`, because the status routes work: absent routes to a contract owner to DEFINE, derivable_with_caveat routes to A6 to COMPUTE, and A6 cannot define another contract's values; and because A-03 has no closed enum under any part of it, so it returns the empty set rather than a coarser number. The benchmark assessor's competing reading — a validating carrier makes derivable_with_caveat arguable — is recorded IN FULL inside the entry. What settles it is a Product Owner ruling on what the status column is for.

Keeping `absent` required AMENDING this document's own definition of `absent`, which spoke only of a missing FIELD. The amendment is declared in source_status_vocabulary.vocabulary_amendment_note rather than made quietly, and the note says plainly that a reader may suspect a definition bent to fit an answer.

M-10 IS THE POPULATION QUESTION THE CORRECTION SURFACED AND CANNOT ANSWER. Nothing states whether a superseding CTR-USG-001 record reuses the superseded record's occurred_at — in which case it falls in the SAME window — or carries its own, in which case it falls in a LATER one. Monthly totals differ between the readings. The populations are stated in a form correct under both; the question belongs to CTR-USG-001's owner (A0 with A6, per RFC-2026-014). It also weakens one premise of a finding made against the withdrawn increment, that C-04 'counts corrections by the month they arrive rather than the month they correct' — true under one reading only. The finding survives in a form that does not depend on the reading and is recorded that way: C-04 cannot distinguish the two, and the withdrawn increment never said which it assumed.

The multi-hop supersession rule and the double-supersession case are DECLARED INFERENCES; no source states either. CTR-USG-001's own annotation records both, and self-reference, as resolver obligations its validator cannot express — and a self-superseding document VALIDATES today (probe USG-SELF-SUPERSESSION-VALIDATES).

Four metrics are proxies with a stated bias direction rather than the metric they resemble: A-02 (cohort start biases upward), A-04 (counts metered attempts, not successes), S-01 (auditability proxy for 'active workspace'), C-04 (blind to a usage record that was never emitted). M-06 named two of the four in the withdrawn increment while its own self-check named four; four is right and all four are now in the canonical file.

There is no single-number cost per workspace. CTR-USG-001 admits THB and USD and its own freeze boundary states currency conversion is not in the contract, so C-01 reports per currency until an FX policy has a rate source, a rate-date convention and an owner. Every cost figure is also GROSS: cost.amount carries no sign, so a superseded record is EXCLUDED rather than netted (probe USG-NO-NEGATIVE-AMOUNT).

Window boundaries are UTC because that is the instant the records carry. CTR-TEN-001.timezone is const Asia/Bangkok and required — not per-tenant and not a guess, which is the M-01 correction — so whether a reporting month is cut on that timezone or on UTC is a FORMULA decision for the Product Owner under OPEN-016 and not a contract gap. The withdrawn increment's citation of OPEN-002 for this is withdrawn.

Four of the five cardinality-budget lines are unenforced, and one of those cannot be enforced at all until CTR-ERR-001.code has a vocabulary. capability_key's per-module ceiling is not expressible in JSON Schema in any case.
Whether these are the right fourteen metrics is a product judgement this run cannot make. They were chosen from what the contracts can support, which is a source constraint.

NEITHER CHECKER IS WIRED INTO npm run check, so nothing runs them automatically when a contract changes under this dictionary. Making them a suite would put test files in test-kits/, which this package does not own. They are package evidence, not repository guards.

One new branch in the strengthened checker is NOT mutation-covered and is named rather than implied: the unresolvedRef path fires only for a $ref this script cannot follow, and every $ref in the shared kernel is the followable sibling form. FOUND BY INDEPENDENT TESTING, recorded rather than fixed, and the most pointed of the three because the whole A-03 argument turns on what a status word means: source.status is NEVER VALIDATED against the document's own source_status_vocabulary. A metric whose status reads "obviously_derivable" -- a word this dictionary defines nowhere -- exits 0. The three defined statuses drive routing (absent goes to a contract owner, derivable_with_caveat goes to A6), so a status outside the vocabulary routes nothing and nothing says so. The next author should close it by checking every source.status against Object.keys(source_status_vocabulary), minus the vocabulary_amendment_note key, which is prose sitting in that object and would have to be excluded.

FOUND BY INDEPENDENT TESTING, recorded rather than fixed: THE FIELD-VERSUS-FORMULA CHECK IS ONE-DIRECTIONAL. It fails when a formula NAMES a field the entry does not declare, and never when an entry DECLARES a field its formula does not name. A formula gutted to a single word, naming none of its seven declared fields, exits 0. Worse for the defect class it was built for: a token that does not resolve against the schema is silently treated as prose, so if C-03's original defect had been a MISSPELLING of occurred_at rather than an omission of it, hole 5 as built would not have caught it -- the misspelling would not resolve, and an unresolvable token is exactly what prose looks like to this check. Closing it needs the reverse direction (every declared field appears somewhere in the formula or population) and a way to tell a misspelled field from an English word, which the backtick convention could carry and does not yet.

THE PIN IS A COUNT, AND "PINNED" READS STRONGER THAN IT IS. EXPECTED_RESOLVED_PATHS catches a field that leaves and a field that arrives, and NOT a compensating pair: remove one citation and add another and the total is still 63 and the run is still green. The script's own header calls it a count and claims nothing more, so this is a matter of how the word reads rather than a false statement, but it is written down here so the next author does not mistake it for a checksum over the citations. A digest of the sorted field list would close it.

It validates PRESENCE and structurally cannot validate an ABSENCE claim — which is exactly how a false `absent` reason shipped on a green run last time. population-and-carrier-probes.mjs is the half that executes the absence claims.

THE HIGHEST-VALUE OBJECTION IS THE ONE THE BENCHMARK NAMES: another over-claim about an adjacent contract. Its own term is that the Author's recommendation is WITHDRAWN rather than re-conditioned if this second sample repeats it. Every negative claim in the document was audited under C3 and either ships with a constructed failing document or was downgraded to 'no contract defines this' — so the way to find a remaining one is to look for a sentence that asserts a limitation WITHOUT a probe id next to it.

The second-highest is A-03's status. Do not accept it because the Author argued for it; the entry records the competing reading in full and states what would settle it. If you think derivable_with_caveat is right, say so — the Product Owner has both readings either way.

Attack the populations. Six metrics now state one, and the whole class of defect is that a population sounds right and is not. C-04's exception (superseded records IN) and C-03's meaning change (a reconciled estimate stops voting) are the two most likely to be wrong.

M-10 is the Author's own unresolved question and the place where an assumption would be most tempting. Check that the populations really are correct under BOTH readings, because that is what is claimed.

Search the dictionary for any number that is not a field count, an enum size, the cardinality budget, or the 20.00/22.00/42.00 of the population demonstration. A leaked target is still the failure this package exists to prevent.
